name: Golf driving range
summary: Ranges span from single-level covered tee lines (tens of thousands of dollars per bay) to multi-level climate-controlled entertainment venues with full kitchens (Drive Shack $25–40M for 72–96 bays; Topgolf $15–60M per venue). Per-bay cost is dominated by the hitting structure, outfield netting/poles and, for entertainment formats, the restaurant/bar building. Entertainment-format costs are sourced from SEC filings; traditional-range costs are derived.

typicalSize.method: Traditional/two-level ranges ~30–60 bays; entertainment venues 72–96 bays (e1) to ~100+. Mid 60.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Building SF per bay: e1 60,000 SF / ~84 bays ≈ 714 SF/bay for entertainment venues (incl. kitchen, bars, event space); covered traditional tee lines ~100–150 SF/bay plus a small clubhouse. Mid 300 for a two-level covered range with clubhouse.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: e1: 72–96 bays on 12–15 acres ≈ 6–7 bays/acre (multi-level, ~200-yd outfield). Single-level ranges with 300-yd fields ≈ 2–4 bays/acre. Mid 4.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Traditional ranges ~1.5–2 spaces per bay; entertainment venues with event space ~3–4 per bay. Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2024 dollars. High: e1 total investment ≈ $387k/bay mid (2021) × ~0.70 hard share (excl. tech, FF&E, soft) ≈ $270k, rounded up for 2021→2024 escalation ≈ $350k for an entertainment venue (e2's $15–60M range is consistent). Mid $110k: two-level covered steel hitting structure (~$40–60k/bay), outfield netting/poles and target greens (~$25–35k/bay at 60 bays), lighting, ball system and a ~3,000–5,000 SF clubhouse (~$25k/bay). Low $30k: single-level covered tee line with netting and lighting. Mid and low are derived, not sourced.

perSF.method: perPrimaryUnit / sfPerPrimaryUnit at each tier (30k/120; 110k/300; 350k/750) — per SF of building/hitting structure; outfield cost is folded in, so not comparable to building $/SF.

scope.notes: Hitting structure/building, outfield grading, target greens, netting and poles, lighting, parking and utilities. Excludes ball-tracking technology (lineItem), FF&E, kitchen equipment, land, soft costs, off-sites.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (30/110 ≈ 0.27); luxury = high/mid (350/110 ≈ 3.2, i.e., entertainment-venue format); premium ≈ climate-controlled two-level with restaurant.

systemSplit.method: Derived: steel hitting structure (05) and netting/pole system (13) dominate the vertical; outfield grading (31) and target greens/synthetic turf/landscape (32) are large; field and structure lighting (26) ≈ 10%; clubhouse finishes/MEP modest. Not sourced.

lineItems.name: Outfield containment netting and poles (60–170 ft)

cost.method: Derived allowance per LF of netting run including poles/foundations; height drives cost. Verify with netting contractor.

lineItems.name: Ball-tracking / game technology per bay (e.g., radar/camera system, screens)

cost.method: Derived allowance per bay; vendor-specific (often licensed).

lineItems.name: Ball dispenser, washer and collection system

cost.method: Derived: dispenser + washer for traditional ranges at the low/mid; automated ball return/sorting for entertainment venues at the high.
Derived $/SF for kitchen/bar building; e1 entertainment venues ~60,000 SF total. Qty defaults to 0 (traditional range).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Bay furniture/heaters, mats, range equipment; entertainment venues add lounge seating, TVs (e1 mentions 300-plus television screens). Derived.

pctOfHard.method: Design-build is common for venues (e2 notes use of design/build contractors); A&E, netting engineering, civil/stormwater for large outfield, permits. Derived.

softCosts.notes: Netting height may require FAA/zoning variances; lighting studies for neighbors.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Traditional single-level hard ~$30k to entertainment-venue total investment ~$556k/bay (e1 high, 2021) plus escalation.

source.title: Drive Shack Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021

evidence.quote: generally open-air 60,000 square feet venues on average built on approximately 12 to 15 acres of land. This format features 72 to 96 climate-controlled bays ... The total investment cost of a new Drive Shack venue ranges from $25 to $40 million.
evidence.scopeNotes: Total investment (building, outfield, tech, FF&E, soft costs; land may be ground-leased or purchased). Per bay ≈ $260k (25M/96) to $556k (40M/72); mid ≈ $387k (32.5M/84).

source.title: Topgolf Callaway Brands Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2023
source.publisher: U.S. SEC EDGAR (Topgolf Callaway Brands Corp.)

evidence.quote: we generally estimate the gross development cost to build a venue to be between $15 million and $60 million depending on the size, location and various other factors.
evidence.scopeNotes: Gross development cost of a Topgolf venue (bay count not stated in the excerpt; venues range from single-level small formats to three-level large formats). Includes building, outfield, technology, FF&E and soft costs.

openQuestions: Need sourced costs for traditional and two-level covered ranges (municipal range rebuild bids).
